title: Duo acceptance: live workspace to collisions
intro: Everything built since the live workspace (Phase E) through organising, Send to Claude, local HTML with the element picker, duo2 parity, Claude editing open documents, and collisions with changes on disk. Open Duo on the fixture workspace first: run `scripts/acceptance/open-duo.sh` in the duo-v2 repo. Fixtures live in ~/DuoAcceptance (rebuild with `scripts/acceptance/fixtures.py --reset`).
setup: In a terminal: `cd ~/repos/duo-v2 && scripts/acceptance/open-duo.sh` (it adds any new fixtures without resetting yours)
duo2 commands: use `~/repos/duo-v2/build/Duo.app/Contents/Helpers/duo2` from a normal terminal, or plain `duo2` inside a Duo session's terminal (or anywhere, once you accept the install question).
Several Send items need a Claude session showing: open checkout and click `+ New session` first.

features.title: Projects come from your folders
features.what: The map shows projects from PROJECT.md files, grouped by their parent folder as topics, with goal, health and next step from the frontmatter.
steps: Look at the All projects map.
features.expect: Topics Growth, Payments, Research; projects onboarding, checkout, refunds, reading with their goals; refunds says At risk · Spec review Oct 8.

features.title: Home is the folder with HOME.md, always running

steps: Look at the left pane on All projects.
features.expect: ★ home with a running Claude Code terminal in `~/DuoAcceptance/workspace/home`.

features.title: + New session
features.what: Starts a Claude Code session in the project folder with a Duo-minted id, filed in the project's `.duo/sessions.json`.
steps: Open checkout.
Click + New session (left pane) or the + in the console tab strip.
features.expect: A new tab opens with Claude Code running in `~/DuoAcceptance/workspace/payments/checkout`.

features.expect: Only to review, working and idle counts. The count returns (in orange) when a session needs you.

Don't answer yet; look at the action column and the toolbar.
features.expect: A card with the verbatim question and options; the toolbar shows 1 need you.

decisions.title: A keyboard shortcut for Send Selection to Claude
context: **Send Selection to Claude** puts the text you've selected (in a Markdown document or an HTML page) into the showing Claude session's prompt, quoted with its file and lines, without sending. Today it's in **Edit › Send Selection to Claude** and on the right-click menu, with no shortcut.
The shortcut map is locked (DL-34): every chord needs a decision. All Duo chords carry ⌘ so they never collide with keys typed into Claude Code. Chords already taken:
`⌘K` jump · `⇧⌘A` search · `⌘↑` All projects · `⇧⌘H` Home · `⇧⌘P` peek · `⌘↩` jump into the peek's selection
`⌃⌘S` sidebar · `⌥⌘0` right pane · `⌥⌘←/→` panes · `⌘N` / `⇧⌘N` new file / folder · `⌘S` save · `⌘B` / `⌘I` bold / italic · `⌘W` / `⇧⌘W` close tab / window

Legacy Duo used **⌘D** for exactly this (its "Send → agent" pill), so your fingers may already know it. ⌘D is free in Duo. In the macOS Save dialog ⌘D means "Don't Save", which can't clash with a document view.
This choice can also be Search's "Send to Claude" shortcut (decision 23e), so one chord means send everywhere.

decisions.title: Search: direct shortcuts on the actions
context: Return runs the main action and Tab opens the actions menu (both yours). The design proposes direct chords so you needn't open the menu:
`⌘↩` Send to Claude · `⌥⌘↩` open in split view (not built) · `⇧⌘↩` open a session read-only at the turn
`⌥⌘C` copy path (files) / copy resume command (sessions) · `⇧⌘C` copy passage · `⌘R` reveal in Finder

**One clash:** `⌘↩` already means "jump into the selected project" in the peek (⇧⌘P). The peek and search are never open together, so it works, but one chord would have two meanings. If you choose ⌘D in decision 22, Send to Claude could be ⌘D here too.
